description: Pure-inference live validation of ml/models/rf_single_event.pkl (Session D, trained 2026-08-10) against freshly captured, independent registration events. No retraining/refitting performed at any point.

devices.realme: Realme RMX3363, adb serial f74439fa, imsi-001010000000004

comparison_to_session_d_baseline.verdict: holds up / improves, not a regression
comparison_to_session_d_baseline.explanation: Live accuracy (99.2%) is well above the Session D full 7-class macro-F1 (0.847), but this is not an apples-to-apples comparison: this validation run only exercised 4 of the 7 trained labels (0,1,3,5), deliberately excluding labels 2/4/6 which are the main sources of confusion for label 0 in the full 7-class CV confusion matrix (label 0 is confused with label 6 in 99/604 CV rows, and with 2/3/4 in 22/23/21 rows respectively; label 1/3/5's CV F1 in isolation were already 1.0/0.859/0.881). Restricting Session D's own CV confusion matrix to predictions among {0,1,3,5} gives 2083/2167 = 96.1% accuracy, much closer to (and still below) the 99.2% observed live. Both live-validation devices (Nothing 3A, Realme) are members of the original 6-profile training set (not held out), so this run tests in-distribution generalisation, not cross-profile transfer; per the project's internal build log's W6.3 LOPO finding, these two profiles specifically generalise well (macro-F1 0.82/0.81) even when fully held out, consistent with strong live performance here. The single miss (1 Realme label-0 row predicted as label 6) is exactly the model's known largest label-0 confusion direction from the Session D CV confusion matrix, not a new failure mode.

investigation.label_imbalance_checked: Ruled out — perfectly balanced, 30 events per label (15 per device), 120 total.
investigation.decode_anomalies_checked: Ruled out — all 120/120 PCAPs decoded cleanly by extract_features.extract() with no TSharkCrashException/truncation fallback triggered (Bug 13/17 class of anomaly), 0 nulls in features/raw_12f_live_validation.csv, and every profile/label combination produced byte-identical feature values across all 15 repeat events (zero within-class variance), matching the deterministic behaviour already documented for these attack labels in the 2026-08-10 Session C2 characterisation.
investigation.distribution_shift_checked: Ruled out — live-captured label-0 feature vectors for both devices were compared directly against features/raw_12f.csv's original training rows for the same profiles: nothing3a (ue_category=16, ca_band_count=1, mimo_dl=4, mimo_ul=1, vonr=True, nr_band_count=10) and realme (ue_category=15, nr_band_count=13, total_capability_size_bytes=813, ie_field_count=11) match the original training data's values exactly, field-for-field. No RF/firmware/carrier-config drift detected between the original Session A/B capture (2026-08-08/09) and this live-validation run (2026-08-11).

operational_note: False negative rate is 0% for all three attack labels tested (1 Cat-downgrade, 3 MIMO-reduced, 5 Combined) — no attack was missed. The single error was a label-0 (Normal) row misclassified as label 6 (Partial/noise), i.e. a false alarm on benign traffic, not a missed attack — the operationally critical failure mode for this study.
